haiku-low.q1: The phone's connection returning, the app coming to the foreground, and every 60 seconds while the phone is online.
haiku-low.q3: The server detects it by comparing the change's base version with the note's current version. A mismatch means conflict.
haiku-low.q4: Note N holds the first-synced phone's text at version 2. The losing phone's text is saved as a new note titled "N title (conflict)".
haiku-low.q5: One outbox entry holding the whole latest note body, with the base version of the first edit.
haiku-low.q6: Each change has a unique change ID. The server saves the result of every processed ID and returns it on retry without reapplying the change.
haiku-low.q7: In the phone's SQLite database, in the same database as the notes. It is updated in the same transaction that applies a downloaded page.
haiku-low.q8: The cursor never moved, so the next sync resumes from the same place. Nothing is skipped or lost.
haiku-low.q9: It learns through its next download, which includes the conflict-note log entry. Its copy of N is replaced with the server's winning text.
haiku-low.q10: Only after the phone receives a result for that change ID from the server.
haiku-low.q12: It goes into a new outbox entry. The already-sent change's contents are fixed and not changed.

sonnet.q1: The phone getting its connection back, the app coming to the foreground, and every 60 seconds while the phone is online.
sonnet.q2: Upload first, then download, always in that order.
sonnet.q3: The server detects it, by comparing the change's base version to the note's current server version; a mismatch is a conflict.
sonnet.q4: The first phone's text wins: the note holds that text at version 2. The second phone's text is saved as a new note titled "<original title> (conflict)". The server does not merge the texts. It also keeps the change log entries and processed change ID records for both.
sonnet.q5: One outbox entry for that note: the whole note body (the latest text, not a diff) with the base version of the first edit, plus its change ID.
sonnet.q6: Each change has a unique change ID created once by the phone and reused on retry. The server checks its processed-change-IDs table. If the ID is there, it returns the saved result and changes nothing.
sonnet.q7: In a cursor stored in the phone's local SQLite database, in the same database as the notes. It is updated in the same local transaction that applies a page of log entries, so both happen or neither does.
sonnet.q8: The cursor did not move, so the next sync resumes from the same place. Nothing is skipped or lost, and re-applying entries is harmless.
sonnet.q9: The upload gets a Conflict result saying N is at version 2. On its download, the phone receives the log entries, including A's winning change and the new conflict note. Its copy of N is replaced with the winning text, and its own edit survives only in the conflict note.
sonnet.q10: Only after the phone receives a result (accepted or conflict) for that change ID.
sonnet.q12: It goes into a new outbox entry, because once a change has been sent its contents are fixed. The document does not say what base version the new entry uses.
